description: TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ parsing and use: an ISO T-separated string, a space-separated string, a date-only string (which takes midnight), epoch seconds, and NULL passing through. It works in a WHERE clause comparing parsed strings, as an INSERT value into a TIMESTAMP_NTZ column, over a VARCHAR column, and in a direct comparison between two parsed timestamps; unparseable text is refused. Converted 1:1 from functions/ToTimestampNtzTest (now retired), which was a BaseJdbcTest whose assertions mostly branched on the JDBC runtime type - Timestamp or LocalDateTime - and then only checked non-null; the converted suite reads TO_VARCHAR and pins the parsed value instead, which is the claim those branches were circling. The epoch-seconds cell keeps the Java's weaker non-null assertion, since the class deliberately did not pin an interpretation for it.

steps.sql: SELECT IFF(TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(1705315845) IS NULL, 'null', 'set') AS ts
CREATE TABLE events (id INTEGER, event_time VARCHAR)
SELECT id FROM events WHERE TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(event_time) > TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ('2024-01-15 00:00:00') ORDER BY id
CREATE TABLE logs (id INTEGER, log_time TIMESTAMP_NTZ)
SELECT TO_VARCHAR(log_time) FROM logs WHERE id = 1
CREATE TABLE raw_data (id INTEGER, ts_string VARCHAR)
SELECT id, TO_VARCHAR(TO_TIMESTAMP_NTZ(ts_string)) AS parsed_ts FROM raw_data ORDER BY id
